title: The Wizard's Cabin
revision_notes: Rev 1.3 (post-release; TestFlight feedback F-012; user decision 2026-07-07) adds CLUE-GATING: code-entry puzzles no longer accept their solution -- even the correct one -- until their gating clue set has been VIEWED in-game. Gated: p01 (four rune marks + grimoire page A; numeral ring optional), p02 (triptych), p03 (Orion window), p04 (slot-shapes clue, self-satisfying/defensive), p14 (recipe page). NOT gated: free pickups, tool-on-hotspot (p05, p06), mechanism completions (p07, p08, p09), automatic bloom (p10), key-on-lock (p11), item combination/apparatus (p12, p13), item-on-state and endgame (p15, p16, p17) -- physical acts, not code entries. Gated attempts replay each puzzle's EXISTING failure grammar with NO tell distinguishing 'gated' from 'wrong' (see clue_gating.no_tell_rule). New: per-node clue_gate fields with rationale, clue_gate edges, top-level clue_gating policy, developer_notes D6 (gate evaluation & stale-correct-input) and D7 (clue-viewed flags persist in save state), one new anti-softlock invariant, example orderings updated with explicit clue-view steps. Branch order-freedom between the workshop and cellar branches and the requirement-based state model are UNCHANGED; clue-viewed flags are ordinary satisfiable requirements. NO solution value, zone, item, D1-D5 behavior, or color-blind rule changed; no new art states required. FLAGGED for user checkpoint: (1) Designer recommends demoting grimoire page A from p01's required gate set to optional (see p01 clue_gate flags); (2) numeral ring excluded from p01's gate (Designer call); (3) p12 left ungated despite recipe support (Designer call, rationale on node).

Rev 1.2 applies user-approved Blind Playtester recommendations R1 (feed-cup theory-magnet defused: ANY inventory item offered at the brass feed cup gets the same categorical terminal-refusal grammar as the cage reach -- new developer_notes D4; D1's block-or-allow decision for the DRAUGHT specifically is unchanged) and R2 (clock de-escalated: cuckoo-crow pops ONCE on first XII only, thereafter visibly inert with a limp broken spring; toy is clearly carved/paint-chipped, not an echo of the live crow -- new developer_notes D5; numeral ring untouched as p01 reference). Also records the playtest-calibrated blind-solve estimate (60-100 min). No puzzle, solution value, zone, or item changed.

Rev 1.1 applied Validator required fixes 1 & 2 (corrected example orderings; beam-at-alcove respecified as a latched derived CONDITION over moonbeam-on AND mirror-at-detent-3, not an event order) plus advisories A3 (brass feed cup as recognized mis-pour target), A6 (edge-list harmonization), and the p11 terminal-refusal annotation. No puzzle, solution value, zone, or item changed.
theme: Abandoned wizard's cabin deep in gloomy woods. Caged crow, potion-making, grimoire, arcane apparatus, hidden cellar.
framing_line: The wizard is gone. The crow remains.
time_of_day: Night, clear sky, visible moon and stars (required by puzzles p02, p03, p08-p10).

win_condition.description: Brew the Unbinding Draught, pour it into the front door's rune basin to wither the thorn-vine seal, then slide the bolt and exit.

clue_gating.purpose: TestFlight F-012: a player solved p01-rune-door before ever seeing the flowerpot's EARTH/III clue and hated it. User decision 2026-07-07: puzzles stay order-free BETWEEN branches, but each code-entry puzzle's input is inert until its clue set has been seen in-game.
clue_gating.viewed_definition: A clue counts as VIEWED the moment its designated close-up view (each gating clue node's viewed_when) has been displayed at least once. No dwell time, no comprehension check, no timers. Multi-instance clues (clu-slot-shapes) count as viewed when ANY one instance is displayed.
clue_gating.persistence: Clue-viewed flags are persistent booleans in the save file (developer_notes D7). They are ordinary satisfiable REQUIREMENTS in the state model, never step-order tracking; branch order-freedom is unchanged.
clue_gating.no_tell_rule: An attempt on a gated puzzle whose gate is unsatisfied produces that puzzle's EXISTING failure grammar, presentation-identical to a wrong-answer attempt. No special sound, animation variant, text, or timing difference may distinguish 'gated' from 'wrong'. Designer AGREES with this recommendation (a distinct 'not yet' tell would leak that the entered value may be correct and would add a second failure vocabulary to a near-wordless game). Residual risk -- a player who legitimately deduced a code without viewing a required clue reads the refusal as a bug -- is mitigated by gating ONLY on clues that carry the code's actual information; the single exception is grimoire page A in p01's gate, which is flagged for the user on that node.
clue_gating.ungated_rationale_class: Free pickups, tool-on-hotspot uses, mechanism completions, key-on-lock, fixed-apparatus uses, item-on-state pours, and the automatic bloom are physical acts, not code entries; gating them would punish legitimate experimentation while preventing no spoiler shortcut.
clue_gating.art_impact: None. The no_tell_rule means gated failures reuse existing failure states; no new visual states are required.

derived_conditions.name: beam-at-alcove
derived_conditions.evaluation: Continuously evaluated boolean over two persistent latched states. TRUE the moment both inputs hold, REGARDLESS of the order in which the player achieved them (the mirror may be set to detent-3 before the shutter is ever cranked open, or after). Both inputs persist (no timers), so once true it stays true. This is a condition, never an event sequence. (Validator required fix 2.)

Reaching into the cage (for a feather or anything else) OR offering any inventory item at the brass feed cup triggers the SAME terminal refusal: the crow snaps once, then turns its back and guards its wing; any offered item returns to inventory unspent. Tone is categorical rejection ('this will never work'), NOT a near-miss 'try again' cue. Repeats replay the identical closed-off pose with no escalation or variation, signaling a dead interaction -- reaching in and feeding are BOTH non-paths (R1). Echoes the recipe's 'freely given' pictogram.

nodes.name: Workshop rune lock
nodes.mechanic: environmental-scavenger + symbol mapping + ordered code entry
nodes.input: Press four rune tiles in sequence.
nodes.derivation: Four element runes hidden around z1, each paired with a Roman numeral I-IV giving press order. Grimoire page A maps runes to element pictograms; mantel clock provides Roman-numeral reference.

clue_gate.gate_behavior: Any four-press sequence completed while the gate is unsatisfied -- including the correct one -- resets the tiles with the same dull knock as a wrong sequence. No tell. Tiles self-reset, so no stale-input case exists (D6).
clue_gate.rationale: F-012 root case: the player solved p01 before ever seeing the flowerpot's EARTH/III clue. The four marks carry the entire code (each pairs its rune glyph with its press-order numeral in close-up). Page A included per user decision 2026-07-07.
flags: FLAG (Designer recommends change at checkpoint): clu-grimoire-elements (page A) maps runes to element PICTOGRAMS but is not informationally necessary -- each mark already pairs its glyph with its numeral, and the door tiles show those same glyphs, so pure glyph-matching + numeral ordering solves p01 without page A. Requiring page A creates the ONLY false-block risk in this revision: a player who found all four marks but never opened page A enters a fully-earned correct answer and gets a 'wrong' knock. Designer recommends gate = four marks only, page A optional. Implemented as user-specified pending the checkpoint ruling (one-line change either way).

FLAG (Designer call, per Producer instruction): clu-clock-numerals EXCLUDED from the gate. Roman numerals I-IV sit at the 'clearly fair' end of the knowledge register; the ring is a backup reference for players who need it, and requiring the clock close-up would add friction and a second false-block vector for the majority who do not.

nodes.failure_behavior: Wrong sequence OR gated attempt: tiles reset with a dull knock, presentation-identical. No lockout.

nodes.name: Moon-phase trapdoor
nodes.mechanic: hidden discovery (move rug) + observation + shape-matching dial code
nodes.input: Three rotary dials, each with eight embossed moon-phase shapes.
nodes.derivation: Triptych paintings: crow count (1/2/3) = dial index; moon shape in that painting = dial value. Waxing vs waning crescents/gibbous are mirrored shapes; exact orientation matters.

clue_gate.gate_behavior: Dials rotate freely at all times; while gated the trapdoor stays shut on ANY setting, including the correct one, and dials retain position -- presentation-identical to the existing wrong-code behavior. No tell. Stale-correct-dials case (correct combo set while gated, triptych viewed later) resolves via D6 re-evaluation on close-up entry.
clue_gate.rationale: The dial code exists ONLY in the triptych -- there is no legitimate no-clue derivation -- so this gate can never block an earned solve. It removes the 1-in-512 lucky spin and spoiler entry.

nodes.failure_behavior: Wrong code OR gated attempt: trapdoor stays shut, presentation-identical. Dials keep position; no lockout.

nodes.name: Astrolabe star plate
nodes.input: Rotate pointer to one of six engraved star-pattern plates.
nodes.solution_fixed: plate-2 (Orion: three aligned belt stars with four shoulder/foot stars)
nodes.derivation: Workshop window sky shows Orion (belt prominent). Match the visible star pattern to plate-2. Recognizing Orion's Belt shortcuts it; pure dot-pattern matching also suffices.

clue_gate.gate_behavior: Pointer rotates freely at all times; while gated the drawer stays shut on ANY plate, including plate-2 -- presentation-identical to a wrong plate. No tell. Stale pointer-already-on-plate-2 case resolves via D6 re-evaluation on close-up entry.
clue_gate.rationale: Six plates invite pure brute force (worst case six taps) -- the strongest shortcut this revision closes. The window close-up is the puzzle's entire evidence base AND sits in the same view as the astrolabe, so the gate costs an intended player nothing. Cannot false-block: even a player who knows Orion cold needs the window to learn Orion is the TARGET.

nodes.failure_behavior: Wrong plate OR gated attempt: drawer stays shut, presentation-identical. No lockout.

nodes.name: Sun-and-moon cabinet
nodes.mechanic: item placement, dual-cue (alchemical symbol + physical shape fit)
nodes.input: Place one item in each of two shaped slots.
nodes.derivation: Alchemy: sun=gold, moon=silver. Redundant non-knowledge path: round ring physically fits round sun recess, crescent-stamped coin fits crescent recess; grimoire page B margin confirms.

clue_gate.logic: all_of (the single clue is satisfied by ANY of its two view instances -- cabinet slot close-up or grimoire page B)
clue_gate.gate_behavior: Placement attempted while gated: item pops back to inventory, presentation-identical to a wrong/swapped placement. In practice the gate is SELF-SATISFYING: seating an item requires the cabinet slot close-up, which IS one of the clue's view instances and marks it viewed on entry.
clue_gate.rationale: Defensive-only gate (documented as borderline, not user-blocking): it exists solely to close any UI path that could seat an item without the close-up (e.g., an inventory drag onto the wide shot). Costs the player literally nothing; per Producer guidance ('slot inspection OR grimoire page B').

nodes.failure_behavior: Wrong/swapped placement OR gated attempt: item pops back out and returns to inventory, presentation-identical. No loss, no lockout.

The scratch marks are a nudge, not the code's sole carrier. Gating this would also complicate the order-free cond-beam-at-alcove contract (ordering C sets the mirror before anything else) for zero anti-spoiler gain.

Developer: implement as a condition check, never an ordered event pair (see developer_notes D2). nodes.name: Free the crow
nodes.input: Use star-bit key on star-shaped cage keyhole; open door.
clues: star keyhole visibly matches star key bit (the rusted decoy key misleads visually in-scene only: it is inspect-only per R6-003, never held, and its close-up shows a snapped plain bit that plainly cannot match the star keyhole)

clue_gate.rationale: Key-on-lock physical act; the star bit visibly matches the star keyhole. Obtaining the key already requires traversing z3/z4, so no shortcut exists to close. The 'freely given' theme is delivered by the refusal grammar (D3/D4), not by a gate; making the correct key inert would directly contradict the terminal-refusal messaging ('this will never work' must stay true only for non-paths).

yields.via: crow flies to rafters, preens, one feather drifts down; crow remains perched for the rest of the level

nodes.notes: VALIDATOR ADVISORY + PLAYTEST R1 APPLIED: the terminal-refusal grammar (crow snaps once, turns its back, guards its wing; identical pose on every repeat, no escalation) covers BOTH reaching into the cage AND offering any inventory item at the brass feed cup -- the 'feed the crow' theory must die fast, not read as 'wrong food, keep trying'. See clu-crow-refusal and developer_notes D3/D4. The draught mis-pour case specifically remains governed by D1.

nodes.name: File silver shavings
nodes.location: anywhere (inventory combination); workbench close-up also accepts it
clues: clu-recipe-page (crescent-metal filed pictogram); spoon bowl is stamped with the same crescent hallmark as the coin, identifying it as silver

clue_gate.rationale: BORDERLINE -- Designer call, flagged for checkpoint: the recipe page motivates this act, and a strict reading of the gating decision could gate it on clu-recipe-page. Kept UNGATED because combining two held tools is experimentation, not code entry (the spoon's crescent hallmark independently identifies it as silver), and its output is harmless in isolation: itm-shavings is useless until p14, which IS gated on the recipe page -- so no spoiler shortcut escapes the system. Gating here would punish a player who reasons 'file + soft metal = shavings' unaided.

nodes.notes: Spoon is not consumed until a successful brew completes; re-filing is impossible only after the draught exists (no longer needed).

clue_gate.rationale: Fixed-apparatus physical act (mortar grinds what is put in it -- that is what mortars do). Same containment argument as p12: itm-paste is inert until the recipe-gated p14.

nodes.name: Brew the Unbinding Draught
nodes.mechanic: procedural apparatus puzzle with fixed parameters; ingredient order-free
nodes.input: Set flame stage; add ingredients in ANY order; stir with ladle (direction + count); release ladle to resolve.
nodes.flame_mechanics: Floor bellows pump raises stage; stages cycle 1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 1. Current stage shown by flame height AND which embossed rim rune (I/II/III) has its ember channel lit.
nodes.derivation: clu-recipe-page: flame pictogram + III; spiral with CCW arrowhead and five dots; three ingredient pictograms.

clue_gate.gate_behavior: Flame pumping, ingredient adding, and stirring all remain freely manipulable while gated; only the RESOLVE (ladle release) is inert: any resolve -- including a fully correct one -- produces the standard gray fizzle with all three ingredients floating up and auto-returning to inventory, presentation-identical to a wrong-parameter failure. No tell. Nothing is consumed (existing p14 invariant), so a gated attempt costs one retry at most; no stale-state case exists because resolve is an explicit act and failure fully resets the pot (D6).
clue_gate.rationale: The brew parameters (flame III, CCW x5 stir) are the level's most code-like values and exist ONLY on the recipe page, so the gate cannot false-block an earned solve. In natural play the gate is almost always pre-satisfied -- the black-feather bookmark makes the recipe the grimoire's landing spread -- but it closes the walkthrough/spoiler path that skips the grimoire entirely.

yields.state: draught-ready (cauldron liquid takes a pearlescent sheen with a slow spiral surface pattern -- pattern, not color, is the success cue)

nodes.failure_behavior: Wrong stir direction/count, wrong flame at resolve, OR gated resolve: gray fizzle puff, all three ingredients float to the surface intact and auto-return to inventory, cauldron reverts to water -- presentation-identical in all three cases. Infinitely retryable; nothing is consumed on failure.
nodes.notes: Playtest R3 (art/dev requirement): the recipe page's CCW spiral and the in-scene cauldron view must be orientation-consistent (both read top-down, same handedness), and the ladle's stir-direction affordance must make CW vs CCW unmistakable from the actual camera angle.

nodes.name: Bottle the draught
nodes.input: Use empty phial on ready cauldron.

clue_gate.rationale: Item-on-state physical act; the pearlescent ready-cauldron and the empty phial are self-evident. The knowledge gate already happened upstream at p14.

nodes.notes: Cauldron remains draught-ready after filling; refills possible. This refill invariant is load-bearing for the feed-cup mis-pour case (developer_notes D1).

nodes.name: Feed the door
nodes.input: Pour phial into the crow's-beak rune basin on the door.
clues: basin sits directly over the vine-wrapped bolt; if crow is freed, it perches on the door lintel above the basin (silent nudge)

clue_gate.rationale: Endgame pour onto the level's central, self-evident affordance (beak-shaped basin over the vine-wrapped bolt, present since minute one). Gating the finale on a re-view would be pure friction.

yields.state: door-unsealed (thorn-vines wither and crumble off the bolt)

nodes.notes: The rune basin is the ONLY pour target that advances state. See developer_notes D1 for the brass feed cup mis-pour case.

clue_gate.rationale: Free action once unsealed; nothing to gate.

yields.beat: the crow flies out over the player's shoulder into the moonlit woods

solve_path_notes.structure: Two parallel mid-game branches after z1: WORKSHOP branch (p01 -> p03 -> p04) and CELLAR branch (p02 -> p06 -> p07; spoon; cage key). They cross-link twice: crank (workshop) is needed for the cellar light shaft; file (workshop) is needed with the cellar spoon. Any interleaving that satisfies the requirement edges is valid.
solve_path_notes.gating_note: Rev 1.3: 'view ...' steps below are the clue-views required by clue_gates -- ordinary satisfiable requirements, inserted where a natural player would take them. Every gating clue sits in the start zone (z1) or in the gated puzzle's own zone, zones never re-lock, and clue viewing is a free repeatable action, so every interleaving that satisfied rev 1.2's edges remains valid once the views are inserted; no rev-1.2 ordering had to be RE-ordered, only annotated. p04's gate is satisfied by the placement interaction itself (cabinet close-up) and needs no separate step.
example_ordering_A: view clu-mark-air/fire/earth/water + grimoire page A (all z1)
example_ordering_B: view clu-mark-air/fire/earth/water + grimoire page A (all z1)
example_ordering_C_mirror_first: p09 (mirror set to detent-3 BEFORE the shutter ever opens)
view clu-mark-air/fire/earth/water + grimoire page A (z1 remains freely reachable -- zones never re-lock)
p08 (cond-beam-at-alcove latches here; mirror was already set)
solve_path_notes.state_model: All progression stored as satisfied-requirement flags (zone unlocked, item held, state on, clue viewed -- rev 1.3) plus derived boolean conditions (see derived_conditions); never as step sequences. cond-beam-at-alcove is the canonical example: an AND over two latched states, order-free by construction (ordering C exercises the mirror-first path). Ingredient-add order in p14 is explicitly order-free; only stir direction/count and flame stage are parameterized.
solve_path_notes.revision_note: Validator required fix 1 applied: ordering A previously listed p04 before its prerequisite p05 and omitted the poker/spoon pickups; both orderings now include all free pickups (Validator's proposed correction of A confirmed by Designer).

developer_notes.topic: Brass feed cup mis-pour of the DRAUGHT (Validator advisory A3) -- RESOLVED 2026-07-04: user chose option (a) BLOCK at the style checkpoint. Implement (a), reusing the D4 refusal grammar; option (b) text retained for context only.
developer_notes.note: The brass feed cup on the crow cage is a plausible mis-pour target for itm-phial-draught. Developer must implement exactly ONE of: (a) BLOCK the pour -- phial-on-cup plays a small crow head-shake and the phial returns to inventory unspent (preferred: zero state churn); or (b) ALLOW it -- draught is spent, cup shows a filled state, and the player refills the phial at the still-draught-ready cauldron (the p15 refill invariant is load-bearing in this case). Either choice is soft-lock-free; do not ship any third behavior. This note governs the DRAUGHT specifically; all other offered items follow D4.

Implement beam-at-alcove strictly as the derived condition defined in derived_conditions: re-evaluate on every change to moonbeam-on or mirror-at-detent-3. Never gate it on the order in which those two were achieved.

The reach-into-cage refusal is terminal in tone (see clu-crow-refusal): same closed-off pose on every repeat, no escalation, no randomized variation that could read as progress toward grabbing a feather.

ANY inventory item offered/dragged onto the brass feed cup (herbs cannot be taken, but e.g. blossom, shavings, paste, feather, coin, ring, keys, spoon, poker) triggers the SAME terminal-refusal grammar as the cage reach: crow snaps once, turns its back, guards its wing; identical pose on every repeat, no escalation; the offered item returns to inventory unspent. There must be NO neutral 'item pops back' response at the cup -- neutrality reads as 'wrong food, keep trying' and sustains the false feeding theory. EXCEPTION: itm-phial-draught follows D1 (if D1 option (a) is chosen, its refusal should reuse this same grammar for consistency).

The XII cuckoo-crow pop fires ONCE per save file: first time the hands are set to XII, the carved toy crow pops briefly with a dry wooden clack, then retreats. Every subsequent XII setting produces the SPENT state: the little door hangs ajar, the toy lies tipped over on a visibly limp/broken spring, no motion, no sound beyond a faint creak. The one-shot flag is a persistent cosmetic latch (saved; never gates progression). The toy must read as a crude carved, paint-chipped TOY -- round body, painted dot eyes -- clearly distinct from the live crow's silhouette so it does not teach 'the clock matters to the crow'. The Roman-numeral ring remains fully readable in all clock states (it is the in-room numeral reference for p01).

Gated puzzles re-evaluate (gate AND solution) on (a) every input-change / explicit-attempt event, exactly as today, AND (b) entry into the puzzle's close-up view. Rule (b) exists for the stale case: a player sets the correct value while gated (trapdoor dials on the right phases, astrolabe pointer already on plate-2), later views the gating clue, then returns -- the puzzle must succeed on arrival without demanding an input wiggle. p01 has no stale case (tiles self-reset on every failure); p14 has none either (resolve is an explicit ladle-release and failure fully resets the pot, returning ingredients). Do NOT add any distinct gated-failure presentation (clue_gating.no_tell_rule); the one accepted cost is that in the rare stale case a previously 'wrong' value silently works on return (accepted with the 2026-07-07 decision).

developer_notes.topic: Clue-viewed flags persist in save state (rev 1.3)
developer_notes.note: One persistent boolean per gating clue node (clu-mark-air, clu-mark-fire, clu-mark-earth, clu-mark-water, clu-grimoire-elements, clu-triptych, clu-window-orion, clu-slot-shapes, clu-recipe-page). SET the first time the clue's viewed_when view is displayed; never cleared; SAVED in the save file alongside requirement flags -- a mid-level save/restore must never re-lock a gate. Multi-instance clue clu-slot-shapes uses a single shared flag set by whichever instance (cabinet slot close-up OR grimoire page B) is displayed first. No dwell-time, tap, or comprehension requirement beyond the view being shown. These flags are ordinary satisfiable requirements; they must not introduce step-order tracking anywhere.

red_herrings.design: Bent, plain-bit key by the door. Tempts use on the front door and cage. Fairness valve: close-up shows the bit is snapped and plain; cage keyhole is visibly star-shaped.

Ready-made potions tempt a shortcut (pour one in the door basin). Bottles are inspectable but stoppered with fused wax; pictogram labels depict unrelated effects (sleep, frost, growth). Differentiated by bottle SHAPE and label pictogram, never by liquid color alone.

Hands are movable; the FIRST XII setting pops a crude carved toy crow once (dry wooden clack, charm beat, no reward); every later XII shows the spent state -- door ajar, toy tipped on a limp broken spring, inert. De-escalated per Playtest R2 so it reads as flavor, not signal; the toy is paint-chipped and round-bodied, clearly NOT the live crow. Not pure noise: the numeral ring is the in-room Roman-numeral reference for p01, so time spent here still pays forward.

Not an item, but the level's biggest theory magnet (Playtest F1): the cup invites a 'feed the crow to get the feather' theory. Defused per R1: every offered item gets the crow's terminal refusal (see D4), so the theory dies on first contact instead of sustaining a food hunt.

Two decoy spreads (a zodiac wheel; an anatomical bird diagram) invite over-reading. Neither encodes anything; the bird diagram softly foreshadows the crow's role. (Validator A4: the zodiac wheel shares a star theme with the astrolabe -- time-cost only; playtest confirmed ~3-4 min, fair. Keep the wheel visually non-systematic: no highlighted constellation.)

anti_softlock_invariants: No consumable is destroyed by a failed attempt anywhere (p14 returns all ingredients on failure; p04 rejects wrong placements back to inventory; feed-cup offers return the item unspent per D4).
itm-poker, itm-file, itm-crank, mirror, winch, bellows, ladle, mortar are reusable and never consumed.
moonbeam-on and mirror-at-detent-3 are persistent latched states (no timers); cond-beam-at-alcove is a derived AND over them, true whenever both hold regardless of achievement order.
Locks (p01, p02, p03) have unlimited attempts, no lockout, dials retain position.
The crow cannot be interacted with harmfully; feather is granted exactly once and cannot be lost (it CAN be added to the cauldron anytime; failed brews return it).
itm-phial-draught can be refilled from the still-ready cauldron (p15 note); this covers the feed-cup mis-pour case if Developer chooses allow-behavior (developer_notes D1).
The clock's one-shot cuckoo pop (D5) is purely cosmetic and never gates progression; spending it changes nothing solvable.

Every clue_gate references only clues located in the start zone (z1) or in the gated puzzle's own zone; zones never re-lock and clue viewing is a free, repeatable, cost-free action -- so whenever a gated puzzle is reachable, its gate is satisfiable. Gated attempts consume nothing (p14's gated fizzle returns all ingredients) and clue-viewed flags persist in the save file (D7). (Rev 1.3.)

visually_necessary_elements.rev_1_3_note: Clue-gating adds NO new visual states (no_tell_rule: gated failures reuse existing failure presentations exactly). This list is unchanged from rev 1.2.

colorblind_safety: Moon phases: pure silhouette shapes, no color reliance.
Element runes: distinct geometric glyphs (triangles/bars), paired with pictograms.
Gold ring vs silver coin: shape (round band vs crescent-stamped disc) + slot shape fit + hallmark stamps; never metal color alone.
Flame stages: height + which embossed numeral rune's ember channel is lit; never flame color alone.
Brew success: spiral surface PATTERN + pearlescent sheen animation, not a color change alone.
Potion-shelf red herrings: distinct bottle shapes + pictogram labels, not liquid color.

designer_difficulty_estimate.validator_score_status: 6.0 is the rev-1.2 official score; Validator to re-score for rev 1.3 (Designer expects it to hold -- see rev_1_3_gating_impact)
designer_difficulty_estimate.blind_solve_estimate: 60-100 min for a first-time player (playtest-calibrated, R6; designer's original 45-75 min superseded)
designer_difficulty_estimate.rev_1_3_gating_impact: Designer estimate: negligible-to-slightly-up (+0.0 to +0.25 on the 10-point scale). Gating changes nothing for a player following intended deduction -- every gating clue lies on the natural solve path and was viewed before its puzzle in the playtest traces. It only removes lucky-guess / brute-force / spoiler shortcuts (chiefly the six-tap brute force on p03 and the 1-in-512 spin on p02) and can add at most one extra failure cycle in the rare stale-input edge cases (D6). Blind-solve time estimate unchanged (60-100 min). Recommend the Validator re-score; Designer expects official 6.0 to hold.
designer_difficulty_estimate.rationale: 17 puzzle nodes, 4 zones (2 nested hidden), two cross-linked parallel branches, one mirrored-shape precision code (p02), one multi-parameter procedure (p14), 4 red herrings + 1 defused theory magnet. No timers, no lockouts.
